I have a new project in simple asp dotnet blazor server. 
This one has to be very pared down. 
It runs on the free tier of a service called v elixir. 

I have the dump.txt in the project files. 
Some ground rules: 
absolutely no third party dependencies 
Microsoft first party dependencies ok 
no css or javascript frameworks 
we write our own css and js 
preferably scoped within the same component 

be very mindful of performance as this needs to run on the free tier. 

that being said, I may have gotten a little to happy with the delete button 
and deleted a bit too much 
can you please write everything that is absolutely essential for the site to function? 

remember no third party css js or any third party dependencies

NEVER EVER EVER write code comments. 
in fact, never, ever write comments at all. 
markdown files such as readme.md are the exception but even these should be as concise and terse as possible.
also please update documentation to match the code

Delivery
Whole project as one tar.gz, unambiguous file placement
Any files to delete on updates called out explicitly
No bespoke sed/patch scripts — full files only for anything that changes
Docs updated alongside code changes
Low verbosity, no code comments

the git repository is at https://github.com/kusl/zen-velixir-run 
and the website is at https://zen.velixir.run/ 


velixir.net - Free .NET web hosting, no card required, forever.Promotion (self.dotnet)

submitted 7 hours ago by VelixirNET

Hey, founder of velixir.net

Just a quick post to bring some awareness to our newer offering of completely free .NET web hosting (along with 10 other languages), we've been around for 8 months now and want to give back to the communities that we're also apart of.

0.25 vCPU, 256MB RAM, 1GB Disk - free for forever. We scale it down to zero when no requests are hitting it, and it'll scale back up as another request is in-flight for it.

I'd love some feedback on the offering and platform, and I'll stick around to answer any questions. Thank you.

Infinite_Track_9210 2 points 4 hours ago 

Hi. Internet. How would it work with a wasm app? I have a website built in Open Silver, that compiles into wasm website and it uses Parse SDK to communicate to our server.

Do you reckon I can host the wasm website there?

    permalinkembedsavereportreply

[–]
VelixirNET[S] 6 points 4 hours ago 

Hey! Yeah that should work fine. OpenSilver compiles to Blazor WebAssembly, so if it's a standalone WASM project you'll just want a small .NET Core host project to serve it (the standard Blazor "hosted" setup), and then it deploys like any other .NET app.

Parse can be hosted on velixir too since it's Node.js, and we natively support it as well.

- Joe

    permalinkembedsaveparentreportreply

[–]
TruePadawan [score hidden] an hour ago 

Can I use this for a SignalR server?

    permalinkembedsavereportreply

[–]
VelixirNET[S] [score hidden] an hour ago 

Yep, WebSockets work out of the box, and the SSE and long-polling fallbacks work too.

If you scale out later, our managed Valkey can work as the Redis backplane.

The free plan works fine too. The only catch is that it sleeps after a while with no traffic, so the first connection after a quiet spell takes a few seconds while it wakes up. Whether that matters depends on your use case. If it does, a paid plan (from €3.49/month) keeps it always on.

- Joe

[–]
spicyeyeballs 0 points 6 hours ago 

How does this compare to the free hosting on azure?

    permalinkembedsavereportreply

[–]
VelixirNET[S] 7 points 5 hours ago 

Good question! Azure's F1 free tier is decent, but it caps you at 60 CPU minutes a day, and once you hit that your app stops until the next day. It also doesn't let you use a custom domain, and you need a card to open an Azure account. Our free app has no daily cap, it sleeps when nobody's using it and wakes on the next request (the first hit takes a few seconds). You get a custom domain with HTTPS, no card, and you can push pretty much any language without a Dockerfile, all on EU servers. To be fair, Azure gives you more RAM (1 GB vs our 256 MB) and lets you run more than one free app, so if you're running something hefty it might suit you better. For a small API, bot or side project though, we're the less fiddly option imo.

- Joe

    permalinkembedsaveparentreportreply

Deploy Your Way
CLI. CI. Or your AI agent.

Four ways in, one pipeline behind them. Whichever you pick, velixir builds your source into a container image and rolls it out in seconds. No Dockerfile, no YAML.

However you deploy

AI agent New

Your agent deploys the app it just built and hands the person a link to keep it. No account needed.
npx -y @velixir/mcp

velixir CLI

One command from your terminal. Nothing to set up first, which makes it the fastest way to try us.
velixir deploy

GitHub Actions

Add one workflow file and every push to your deploy branch ships a release. All it needs is an API key, with no App to install on your repo.
.github/workflows/velixir.yml

Any other CI

Azure DevOps, GitLab, Jenkins, whatever you already run. The CLI is the deploy step.
- run: velixir deploy

All four run the same pipeline
terminal
$ velixir deploy
▸ Packaging source (1.1s)
▸ Building image (Node 22)
▸ Pushing image (myapp-api:v1 → registry)
▸ Deploying to eu-central (primary · 3 replicas)
▸ Autoscaling configured (min: 2, max: 10)
▸ Edge routes published (TLS provisioned, custom domains live)
✓ Live at myapp-api.velixir.run (4.2s)
Platform Features
Everything your app needs. Nothing it doesn't.

Every request reaches you through velixir's own edge nodes in the EU. Everything behind them, from the build to the bandwidth, is ours to run.

In front of your app

A visitor

or a bot, or a scanner

TLS

Certificates issued and renewed for you, custom domains included.

Rate limiting

Per-IP request and connection caps, set per app, live with no redeploy. Over the limit gets a 429 here.

Managed WAF

The OWASP Core Rule Set. Watch in detect mode first, then switch to blocking.

Under-attack check

Every browser solves a proof of work. Seconds for a person, ruinous for a botnet.

Your app

Plain HTTP on the port we hand you. Nothing to install, nothing to configure.

Dashed stages are yours to switch on, per app, whenever you need them.

Behind your app

Immutable releases

Your source becomes a container image once, so scaling out is a pull and start, never a rebuild. Preview in staging, then roll back to any earlier image in seconds.

Autoscaling

Min and max instances per app, scaled on CPU with defaults that already work. Up on demand, back down when the demand goes.

Managed compute

Capacity, patching and node-level failover are ours, on velixir-run hardware in the EU.

Unmetered bandwidth

No egress fees and no per-GB meter, so a busy launch day never lands as a surprise on the bill. A soft fair-use guideline keeps one app from crowding out the rest.
Any Language
Any language.
Built and run for you.

velixir isn't tied to one framework. Push your source and we build it into a container image, then run it with autoscaling and high availability. Node.js, Python, Go, Ruby, PHP, Java, Elixir, Rust, Deno, F#, and .NET are all first-class.

    Automatic builds from source, no Dockerfile
    Node.js, Python, Go, Ruby, PHP, Java, Elixir, Rust, Deno, F#, and .NET (Core 1.0 through .NET 10)

    Lift-and-shift an existing app or start greenfield in any supported runtime

Debug with AI
Your deploy failed.
Here's why, in English.

The worst part of a first deploy going wrong is not the error. It's not knowing which line of four hundred is the one that matters. Press Explain this on your logs and you get the cause in a sentence, the fix as steps, and the exact lines it read.

    It knows how velixir runs your app, so it catches the port and binding mistakes a generic assistant guesses at.
    It quotes the log lines behind every answer, so you can check the reasoning instead of trusting it.
    Runs on a European model, only when you press the button, and never sees your environment variable values.

How it works
Runtime Logs Live
Explain this

Your app is listening on 127.0.0.1, so nothing outside it can get in.
Confident

    Bind to 0.0.0.0 instead of localhost.
    Read the port from the PORT environment variable rather than hardcoding 3000.

Log lines this is based on
10:42:01 Server started
10:42:01 listening on 127.0.0.1:3000
10:42:14 health check failed: connection refused
10:42:29 CrashLoopBackOff
High Availability
A node goes dark. Your app doesn't.

Turn HA on and we keep warm standby replicas on separate worker nodes. Watch what happens when the primary stops answering.
Primary probe fails
Primary cluster stops responding.

The edge tries the primary pool with a 500 ms connect budget. Two backends fail in a row - the per-hostname circuit-breaker trips for 3 minutes.

Pick the standby's plan and replica count separately from production, so insurance does not cost the same as the thing it insures.
European sovereignty, by default
One region.
In Europe. On purpose.

Every app, database, and cache runs in EU Central. Your data stays under European jurisdiction and never leaves the EU. It is not a setting you switch on, it is the only place we run.
